title: PIM for Active Directory: prepare Active Directory for the hybrid worker
purpose: Prepares Active Directory for the PIM for Active Directory hybrid worker: its group managed service accounts, their least-privilege rights, the servers GPO and, for an Azure VM, the offline domain-join blob.
whenToRun: Once per worker, by the AD administrator on a domain controller (or a domain-joined admin host with dsacls.exe and the Group Policy Management tools), after the infrastructure step. Re-run safely after changing OUs or adding server onboarding.

runAs.name: Domain Admins
runAs.why: creates gMSAs, groups and the servers GPO, and delegates OU rights (dsacls)

runAs.name: Enterprise Admins (only with -CreateKdsRootKey)
runAs.why: creates the forest's KDS root key

changes.object: per identity: the gMSA (AES256), <name>-PermissionGroup (the gMSA its only member) and <name>-PrincipalsAllowedAccess (the worker computer)
changes.why: AD is written only by gMSAs, one per privilege tier; every right goes to the PermissionGroup
changes.undo: delete the gMSAs and their two groups

changes.object: ACEs for <GmsaName>-PermissionGroup: -GroupsOu read + create groups + write member/displayName/description; each -AdminAccountsOu create users + full control below; AdminSDHolder write member only with -GrantProtectedGroupMembership (Tier 0)
a GPO (Restricted Groups: <ServerGmsaName>-PermissionGroup member of BUILTIN\Administrators, adds only) linked to each -ServerOu
changes.why: server onboarding by the Tier-1 identity

changes.object: the worker's computer account in -ComputerOu and the offline domain-join blob (printed)
changes.why: joins the Azure VM without line of sight; an Azure Arc server is already joined

changes.object: a KDS root key (Add-KdsRootKey), usable about 10 hours later

parameters.name: WorkerComputerName
parameters.help: The worker's computer name (Azure VM name or the Arc server's name).

parameters.name: ComputerOu
parameters.help: The OU of the worker's computer account.

parameters.name: GmsaOu
parameters.help: Where the gMSAs and their groups are created.

parameters.name: GroupsOu
parameters.help: Where PIM creates and maintains AD groups.

parameters.name: AdminAccountsOu
parameters.help: OU(s) of the AD admin accounts PIM creates.

parameters.name: GrantProtectedGroupMembership
parameters.help: Write member on AdminSDHolder (protected groups) -- the worker becomes Tier 0.

parameters.name: ServerGmsaName
parameters.help: The Tier-1 server onboarding identity; needs -ServerOu.

parameters.name: ServerOu
parameters.help: The servers OU(s) for the GPO. Keep the worker out of them (the script warns).

parameters.name: ServerAdminGpoName
parameters.default: PIM for AD: <ServerGmsaName>-PermissionGroup is local administrator (servers)

parameters.name: UsedBy
parameters.help: Text written into the gMSA descriptions.

parameters.name: ProvisionOdj
parameters.help: Azure VM: create the computer account and print the offline domain-join blob.

parameters.name: ReuseComputer
parameters.help: With -ProvisionOdj: re-provision an existing computer account (resets its password).

parameters.name: CreateKdsRootKey
parameters.help: Create the forest's KDS root key when there is none (usable ~10 hours later; the script prints when).

parameters.name: TriggerSdProp
parameters.help: Apply AdminSDHolder on the PDC emulator now instead of within the hour.

readsOnly: the domain (RootDSE, partitions), the OUs, existing gMSAs / groups / computer, the KDS root keys and their age, the AD Privileged Access Management feature (detected, never enabled), the GPO and its links
network: the domain controllers only (LDAP through .NET System.DirectoryServices, dsacls.exe, djoin.exe, SYSVOL); no internet. Modules: only the owner-approved Windows GroupPolicy module (to create the GPO) and Add-KdsRootKey (with -CreateKdsRootKey), framework 12.17
whatIf: Prints every object, right, GPO setting and link it would create; creates nothing.
undo: Unlink and delete the servers GPO, remove the ACEs (dsacls <dn> /R <DOMAIN>\<GmsaName>-PermissionGroup) on -GroupsOu, each -AdminAccountsOu and AdminSDHolder, then delete the gMSAs, their groups and (for an Azure VM) the computer account.
